note: Fifty-six verses, and structurally unlike every other book in the index so far: it opens as a complaint against God, receives an answer that makes the complaint worse, complains again, and is then told to wait. Nothing is resolved within the book. What changes is the man.
genre_note: Prophetic, but addressed upward rather than outward. Micah indicts a people on God's behalf; Habakkuk indicts God on the people's behalf and is answered rather than rebuked. That difference matters for Sacred Lament: the practice is not merely permitted here, it is the form the entire book takes, and it is met with a reply.

entries.pericope: How long will I cry, and you will not hear?
entries.connection: The book opens by accusing God of not listening, and the complaint is preserved as scripture rather than corrected. Sacred Lament in its least decorous form — not grief brought to God but a charge laid against him, and the charge is that justice never goes forth.

entries.pericope: I am working a work you would not believe
entries.connection: The answer to the complaint is an announcement that God is doing something the hearer would not believe if told — and it turns out to be worse than the problem. The Discipline of Unknowing at its hardest: the reply is real, and it does not relieve.

entries.pericope: You who are of purer eyes than to see evil
entries.connection: The second complaint is sharper than the first and argues from God's own character against God's own action. The prophet does not moderate after being answered, which establishes that lament may continue after a reply has been given and been found insufficient.

entries.pericope: I will stand at my watch and set myself on the ramparts
entries.connection: The watchman image C20 is named for, in its original setting and enacted rather than commanded. He posts himself deliberately to see what will be said and what he will answer — watchfulness directed at receiving a reply he expects to have to respond to.

entries.pericope: Though it delays, wait for it; the righteous will live by his faith
entries.connection: The vision is given an appointed time, and the instruction attached is to wait through the delay rather than to act. The Discipline of Gradualism with its cost stated: the waiting is commanded precisely because the thing looks late, and living by faith is what one does in the interval.

entries.pericope: Woe to him who increases what is not his
entries.connection: Desire is described as enlarged like Sheol and never satisfied, and the plunderer is told his own debtors will rise. Holy Detachment argued from the mechanics of accumulation rather than from piety — what is gathered this way is on loan.

entries.pericope: The stone will cry out of the wall
entries.connection: A house built by evil gain testifies against its builder — the stone from the wall and the beam from the woodwork answering each other. C01's moral order given a physical voice: the structure itself is a witness.

entries.pericope: The earth will be filled with the knowledge of his glory
entries.connection: Set immediately after a woe against a city built with blood: the peoples labour only for the fire, and the earth fills with knowledge as waters cover the sea. The end state named in the middle of the indictment rather than after it.

entries.pericope: Woe to him who gives his neighbor drink
entries.connection: Harm done through hospitality — the cup pressed on a neighbour in order to expose him. Injury delivered by an act that looks like generosity, which is the hardest kind for a community to name.

entries.pericope: Let all the earth be silent before him
entries.connection: The idol is called a teacher of lies because it cannot answer, and the contrast offered is not a louder voice but silence before one who can. After two chapters of argument the instruction is to stop talking — the recognition that reality exceeds one's grasp of it, enacted rather than conceded.
entries.review: PR04 added at review. The definition is Ephrem's posture — the disciplined recognition that reality exceeds your grasp — and silence commanded at the end of two chapters of questioning is exactly that, enacted. Accepted on the definition, not the name.

entries.connection: Having demanded justice for two chapters, he now asks that judgment be tempered. The petition reverses his own opening complaint, and the reversal is the point: mercy is asked for by the man who was demanding the wicked be dealt with.

entries.pericope: God came from Teman; rays where his power is hidden
entries.connection: A theophany recounted in the past tense as the ground for present endurance, with power described as hidden inside the light rather than displayed by it. Remembered acts doing the work that an answer to the complaint did not.

entries.pericope: Though the fig tree doesn't flourish, yet I will rejoice
entries.connection: His body trembles and rottenness enters his bones, and the joy is declared in the same breath rather than after the trembling stops. Every crop is listed as failing before the yet, so nothing has improved between the first verse of the book and the last — which makes this the clearest statement in Scripture that lament and rejoicing are not sequential stages.

review_log.adjudication: Clean pass. One gap addition proposed on 2:18-20 and accepted: PR04.
